en.pageTitle: LSC Player: accessible video in Sign Language - Diego Mena
en.cardTitle: Reproductor LSC: educational HTML5 video in Colombian Sign Language
en.cardDesc: Accessible HTML5 educational player in Colombian Sign Language (LSC) with multi-camera synchronization, A-B loop repetition and interactive glossary with self-assessment.

articles.article12-p1: For the Colombian deaf community, Colombian Sign Language (LSC) is the first language and written Spanish is a second language. A conventional video player is not enough to learn it: you need to see the sign from multiple angles, repeat fragments and consult the glossary. Reproductor LSC was built for that.
articles.article12-p2: Signing is three-dimensional: it involves hands, facial expression and body orientation. The player plays two or more video streams in perfect sync (front and side), allowing views to be switched or combined without losing the temporal point, something that requires precise control of the HTMLMediaElement API.
articles.article12-p3: Learning a sign demands repetition. A-B loop mode lets you mark a start and end point and replay that fragment in a cycle, without intervention, until the production is mastered. The control is exposed to both mouse and keyboard, with live-region announcements of the selected range.
articles.article12-p4: The pedagogical component is completed with a browsable sign glossary and a self-assessment mode that hides the gloss and challenges the student to recognize the displayed sign. Results are announced in a role="status" region to preserve context.
articles.article12-p5: The player's own interface fulfills the principles it preaches: native keyboard-operable controls, visible focus, labels in Spanish and LSC, and screen reader compatibility. The goal is for the tool to serve hearing teachers and deaf students alike.
articles.article12-p6: The project is open source at github.com/ingelectronicadj/ReproductorLSC.
